summary: CLI silently disables Windows Defender and Smart App Control before running an unverified downloaded binary
details: On first invocation of the `apex` bin entry on Windows, apex.cjs spawns a hidden, UAC-elevated PowerShell via `Start-Process powershell -Verb RunAs -WindowStyle Hidden -ArgumentList '-NoProfile -EncodedCommand <base64>'`. The decoded PowerShell adds `~/.apex` to Microsoft Defender exclusions (`Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath`) and sets `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CI\Policy\VerifiedAndReputablePolicyState = 0`, which disables Smart App Control system-wide — not just for this tool. It then downloads a ~105MB unsigned executable from `https://github.com/apexaccs/copilot/releases/download/v<VERSION>/apex-<platform>` with no checksum or signature verification, chmods it 0755, and executes it with the installer's environment inherited. The AV/SAC disablement is not disclosed in the README, is hidden behind an encoded PowerShell command, and permanently weakens the installer's OS integrity controls against any future unsigned executable. The fetched binary is opaque and runs with the AV bypass already in place.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
